full_judgment: 5. The appellant Court below found that there was no dispute between the parties that Azhar Ali got in his share .7 acres in plot No. 197, khatian No. 3. The dispute is whether Hamid Ali got .7 acres in plot No. 202, khatian No. 5, as claimed by the plaintiff or .7 acres of land in plot No. 192 No. 46, as claimed by the defendants Khatian No. 46 was exhibited by the plaintiff. The appellate Court below found that the plaintiff could not give any personal knowledge of the amicable partition and P.W. 3 Hafizullah and P.W. 8 Bashirullah also could not give proper relevant answers relating to partition in their cross-examination. The appellate Court below found that in khatian No. 46 there are 2.58 acres of land and Azhar Ali is the owner by purchase in respect of .83 acres of land therein. In this khatian Hamid Ali had no ownership. The appellant Court below noted the case of the defendants that Hamid Ali obtained .7 acres of land from khatian No. 46, plot No. 192. P.W. 8 Bashirullah, son of Hamid Ali admitted in his cross-examination that his father Hamid Ali used to possess .7 acres of land of khatian No. 46, plot No. 192 and that the said land is now being possessed by Abdul Gani. That is precisely the case of the defendants and the appellate Court below found that this admission by P.W. 8 weakened the case of the plaintiff The appellate Court below then considered Ext. 5 series, which were earlier considered by the trial Court and found that by Ext. 5 series the sons of Azhar Ali sold the land of plot No. 197, khatian No. 3 and also other lands of khatian No. 46 to various persons. In view of the fact that the defendants admit Azhar Ali's share in plot No. 197, khatian No. 3 and in view of the fact that Azhar Ali had independent title to .83 acres of land in khatian No. 46 the appellate Court below, contrary to the finding of the trial Court, found that Ext. 5 series do not support the plaintiff's case at all. The appellant Court below also held that since there was no partition by metes and bounds the recording of the land of khatian No. 5 in the name of Bashirullah and the mutation of it in favour of the plaintiff does not create any presumption. The defendants title thereto have not been injured thereby.
